_description: Hi Marley product knowledge that informs release impact scanning. Add rules here as you learn them — they are injected into every per-article analysis. Use plain English. The more specific the better.
releaseToDocRules: Hi Marley Inbox is a web app feature for adjusters/operators only. Changes to inbox behavior, inbox badges, inbox notifications (Snooze, Dismiss for Myself, No Response Needed, Address Case) do NOT require updates to integration documentation, API reference articles, webhook guides, or partner setup guides (ClaimCenter, Guidewire, Salesforce, Mitchell, etc.) — UNLESS the release explicitly states that the API payload or webhook event for those features is changing.

Changes to the Hi Marley Web App UI (inbox layout, case badges, notification options, filters, templates, operator settings) affect operator-facing Help Center articles only. They do not affect: API action articles, webhook action articles, SSO configuration guides, or third-party integration setup guides.

Changes to policyholder-facing features (opt-in/opt-out keywords, welcome messages, texting consent) affect policyholder-facing articles and opt-in workflow articles only. They do not affect: integration setup articles, API docs, or operator workflow guides.

Changes to Admin/Organization settings (feature flags, LOB configuration, auto-close rules, team management) affect admin settings articles only. They do not affect: integration articles, API docs, or general operator workflow guides.

A release that adds a new operator notification option (like 'Dismiss for Myself' or 'No Response Needed') should update the Inbox article and any article that documents notification behavior — not API docs or integration guides.

The Integrations Help Center category and the Partners category contain articles for IT teams and developers. These should only be updated when a release explicitly changes: API endpoints, webhook payloads, SSO behavior, or the setup/configuration steps of a specific third-party integration.

The 'Accelerators' section (under Release Information) contains deployment guides for enterprise implementations. These are only affected by releases that change installation steps, predeployment configurations, or enterprise setup requirements.

Notification settings and badge settings are generally specific to the web app, and therefore updates or mentions of notifications and/or badge behavior may be relevant to Inbox-related articles or mobile app articles, but sections and articles related to Integrations likely don't need to be called out as affected, unless it is specific to integrations. Some Partner Integrations do send their own notifications, and they should only be flagged as needing update if the release notes specifically call out that partner integration.

Any reference to "the UI" infers a change specifically to the web app, and therefore likely does not affect articles in the Integrations section unless they're specifically called out. Some Parter Integrations do have UI components though.

When release notes mention a feature becoming "GA" or "generally available", search for an existing article on that feature (it likely exists from the beta). The article should be updated to: (1) remove any '(Beta)' label from the article title, (2) remove beta disclaimers and limited-availability notices, (3) update the availability/prerequisites section to say it's now available to all qualifying customers, and (4) document any new configuration options or behaviors added at GA. Do NOT create a new article if a beta article already exists — update it.
Anything in the "New Features" section of the release notes is of course likely new, and therefore more likely to need a net new article instead of an update to an existing article.

Bug fixes in release notes generally do NOT require Help Center article updates unless the fix corrects behavior that was previously documented as the intended way the feature works. Pure UI display bugs, dropdown filtering bugs, or back-end data bugs rarely need documentation changes. Only flag a bug fix as requiring an article update if it changes a user-facing workflow that is explicitly described in a Help Center article.
For users and organizations using integrations who are using the optional prefix field, "contactPrefix": "Mr." is the correct format, rather than "prefix": "Mr."

As of Release 2.85, here is how away messages will change: 

Carrier admins are now able to set a default Out of Office message and default status (enabled/disabled) for their
organization which is applied across their org for all new users​

Individual operators (users) can change their Out of Office message and status from the organization defaults, and set
them back again, if needed​

When setting their status to “Away”, operators are no longer required to provide and send an Out of Office message
since the messages can be disabled.​

When away, a banner will display across the Hi Marley app and Connect displaying the status and first 50 characters
of the Out of Office message.​

Operators can easily click the banner or toggle buttons to change their Away status or Out of Office message/settings.​

The Feature Audit Log is a completely independent feature of the Audit Log (or Case Audit Log). The Feature Audit Log is within Settings, and only System Admins have access to it, it's a feature that tells System Admins what features have been enabled or disabled in their organization. 

The Audit Log is a feature that within each case allows any user to see any action performed on that case.

Address Case (also called Unaddressed) and Unread are TWO MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE inbox notification modes — organizations choose ONE, and enabling one replaces the other. They do NOT run simultaneously, and Address Case does NOT supplement Unread indicators. When updating any article that references 'Unread' inbox behavior, always add a note that organizations may instead use Address Case, and vice versa — so readers understand both options exist and their org may use either. NEVER write that Address Case 'supplements' or 'adds to' Unread indicators. Instead write: 'Depending on your organization's inbox settings, you may see either Unread indicators or Address Case indicators.' The correct framing is a binary organizational choice between the two modes.

Changes to Away Status, Away Message, or Out of Office behavior ALWAYS affect two specific articles: (1) 'Managing Your Personal Settings' — the operator-facing article documenting personal settings including the away status toggle and Out of Office message, accessible from the profile avatar dropdown; (2) the 'Auto Replies' article — documenting Out of Office / auto-reply message behavior and configuration. ALWAYS search for and flag BOTH articles when a release changes away status, away message, Out of Office defaults, or the behavior/optionality of sending an auto-reply. Use search queries: 'away status', 'auto replies', 'out of office', 'away message', 'personal settings'.

IMPORTANT — 'Managing Your Personal Settings' is an OPERATOR/ADJUSTER UI article, NOT an Admin/Settings article, even though the title contains 'settings'. It documents personal preferences for individual operators: away status controls, notification preferences, profile display settings, and the personal settings dropdown accessible from the profile avatar. Any release that changes the personal settings dropdown, away status workflow, or operator-level notification preferences MUST check and potentially flag this article. It is in the OPERATOR/ADJUSTER domain, not the ADMIN domain.

When a release note names a specific UI element that has changed — a dropdown menu, button, toggle, modal dialog, sidebar panel, status indicator, profile avatar, or similar interactive element — set screenshotUpdateNeeded: true for any article recommendation that documents that area of the UI. A named UI element change is a reliable signal that existing article screenshots showing that element are outdated.

When a release adds a new field to the Contact details pane or Case details pane in the Hi Marley web app (e.g., adding Zip/Postal Code, prefix, custom fields, or any new data field visible in the side panel), flag ANY article that: (1) contains a screenshot of the contact or case details pane, (2) lists or enumerates what fields are available or editable in the details pane, or (3) describes how to view or update contact information. The details pane displays contact fields like name, phone, email, zip code, prefix, etc., so adding any new field is always a screenshot update AND a list/text update for articles that document those fields. Use search queries like 'contact details', 'case details', 'contact information', 'details pane' for features that add fields to the contact or case view.

Public API Authentication and Managing OAuth Credentials should probably fall under one article for the sake of convenience for users. Previously Auto Doc Pilot recommended creating an article for both based on the 2.85 release notes, and while we definitely should have both documented, they probably fall under one article.

IMPORTANT EXCEPTION to 'do not flag API docs for UI changes': When a release adds a NEW FIELD to the Contact or Case data model (e.g., Contact Prefix, zip code, a new custom field), that field also appears in webhook payloads and API responses — so the change DOES affect API/webhook documentation. Always search for and flag webhook event articles (especially 'Contact Updated', 'Case Created', 'Case Updated') when a new contact or case field is introduced. Use search queries like 'contact updated webhook', 'contact API', 'event ID contact', 'webhook payload'. The correct payload field name for Contact Prefix is 'contactPrefix' (e.g., "contactPrefix": "Mr."), not 'prefix'. This exception applies only to data model field additions — purely UI/behavioral changes (inbox layout, notification options, badge behavior) still do NOT affect API docs.

When a release adds a new opt-in keyword (such as 'oui', 'si', or any language variant of 'yes'), always flag the 'Opt-in & Opt-Out Workflow for Texting' article because it enumerates the accepted opt-in keywords. Use search queries: 'opt-in', 'opt-out', 'opt in keyword', 'texting', 'text messaging consent'.

When a release introduces a new messaging token (such as $claimantprefix, $firstname, $lastname, $policynum, or any $-prefixed variable), ALWAYS flag the Message Templates and/or Message Template Tokens article, because it lists all available tokens with descriptions. Use search queries: 'message template tokens', 'message tokens', 'template variables', 'dynamic tokens', 'message templates'. New tokens always need to be added to this reference list. The specific token name (e.g., '$claimantprefix') should also be used as a search query.

Anytime the payload changes for a feature related to a webhook or an API, we should probably review any article that references that object. For example, when we add a Contact Prefix, any time a Contact is created or updated in the API, that likely uses a Contact object in the request payload and therefore Contact API Actions like Update Contacts may change, and therefore the relevant articles should be flagged as potentially needing to be changed.
